specification.problem: Estimate an unknown phase \phi of a single-qubit phase gate U_\phi using a total budget of N gate applications distributed over M qubits prepared in a product state (generalized Kitaev phase estimation), and quantify the Bayesian mean square error of the resulting estimator.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One finite construction: M qubits each prepared in |+>, qubit j receives n_j applications of U_\phi with \sum_j n_j = N, each qubit is measured independently after a local phase shift \theta_j and a Hadamard, and \phi is estimated by Bayesian postprocessing with a flat prior. Tiny explicit instance (assumption): M=2, N=3, (n_1,n_2)=(1,2), (\theta_1,\theta_2)=(0,\pi/2). Outside scope: derivation of the optimal distribution {n_j}, the proof of near-optimality against the Bayesian bound, the loss analysis, comparison with entangled strategies, and the alternative resource quantification for Shor's algorithm.

Estimator of \phi from the outcome string x=(x_1,...,x_M)

equations.label: Product probe state after distributed phase gates
equations.description: Each of the M qubits starts in |+> and accumulates phase n_j\phi after n_j applications of the phase gate; the distribution {n_j} is arbitrary subject to the total budget N. Standard Kitaev corresponds to n_j = 2^{j-1}.
equations.abstract_quote: $N$ phase gates, acting on $M$ qubits prepared in a product state, may be distributed in an arbitrary way
equations.justification: Direct formalization of 'N phase gates distributed arbitrarily over M qubits in a product state'; the |+> initial state and diag(1,e^{i\phi}) gate are the standard Kitaev choice, not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Phase gate acts as diag(1, e^{i\phi}) on each qubit

equations.label: Local measurement statistics
equations.description: Probability of outcome x_j when qubit j is measured after applying the phase shift diag(1,e^{i\theta_j}) followed by a Hadamard; outcomes on different qubits are independent because the state is a product.
equations.justification: Born rule applied to eq_1 with the standard Kitaev X/Y-type measurement; exact equality.
assumptions: Measurements are local, non-adaptive, fixed phases \theta_j

equations.label: Bayesian estimation and cost
equations.description: Flat-prior Bayesian posterior and average cost of the estimator over outcomes and prior. The cost C is the squared error (\tilde\phi-\phi)^2 or its periodic variant 4\sin^2((\tilde\phi-\phi)/2); which one the paper uses is not stated in the abstract.
equations.justification: Standard Bayesian phase-estimation framework consistent with the abstract's reference to 'mean square error' and 'the fundamental Bayesian estimation bound'.
assumptions: Cost function form (MSE vs. periodic 4\sin^2) is a choice

equations.label: Error scaling claims
equations.description: Asymptotic (not exact) scaling: the standard Kitaev distribution yields mean square error scaling as 1/N, while the optimal distribution over the product state achieves Heisenberg 1/N^2 scaling. Constants c_1, c_2 are not given in the abstract.
equations.abstract_quote: Unlike the standard algorithm, where the mean square error scales as $1/N$, the optimal generalizations offer the Heisenberg $1/N^{2}$ error scaling
equations.justification: Stated directly in the abstract as asymptotic scaling statements.
assumptions: Scaling is asymptotic in N; prefactors unknown

equations.label: Fundamental Bayesian bound for N gate uses (reference)
equations.description: Known asymptotic optimal Bayesian cost (periodic cost, flat prior) achievable with an optimal entangled N-gate probe; the abstract claims the optimal product-state generalization comes very close to this bound.
equations.justification: Recalled background result for optimal Bayesian single-phase estimation with N uses; exact constant depends on the cost function and is asymptotic, not an abstract-sourced value.

equations.label: Tiny explicit instance
equations.description: Smallest nontrivial distribution of N=3 gates over M=2 qubits with one X-basis and one Y-basis measurement; the likelihood follows from eq_2.
equations.justification: Chosen as a minimal concrete instance for circuit generation; not specified by the abstract.

registers.name: q
registers.role: Probe qubits, qubit j receives n_j phase-gate applications and is measured locally

steps.description: Prepare each of the M qubits in |+> via Hadamard on |0>.
Apply the phase gate U_\phi n_j times to qubit j, with \sum_j n_j = N (instance: 1 application on qubit 1, 2 on qubit 2).
Apply the local phase shift diag(1,e^{i\theta_j}) and a Hadamard to each qubit, then measure in the computational basis.
Repeat the experiment or use the single-shot outcome string in a Bayesian update with flat prior and compute the estimator minimizing the average cost.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of every qubit after the local phase shift \theta_j and Hadamard; outcome string x \in \{0,1\}^M with likelihood given by eq_2.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute the flat-prior posterior p(\phi|x) from eq_3, output the Bayes estimator \tilde\phi(x) (e.g. the circular mean of the posterior for the periodic cost), and evaluate the average cost \Delta^2; compare scaling in N against eq_4 and eq_5.
assumptions: Initial product state |+>^{\otimes M} and phase gate diag(1,e^{i\phi}) as in standard Kitaev phase estimation
Measurements are local, non-adaptive, with fixed phases \theta_j in {0, \pi/2}
Flat prior and a squared-error or periodic squared-error cost function
Tiny instance M=2, N=3, (n_1,n_2)=(1,2), (\theta_1,\theta_2)=(0,\pi/2) chosen by the reconstruction, not the paper
